I remember the day I learned that everything has a name. My teacher spelled a word into my hand, over and over, and I imitated the motions without understanding that they meant anything. Then she held my hand under a stream of cool water and spelled the word again, and something awoke in me. The mystery of language was suddenly clear. That living word set my soul free; it gave me light, hope, joy. I left the pump-house eager to learn. Everything had a name, and each name gave birth to a new thought. As we returned to the house, every object I touched seemed to quiver with life — because I saw everything with the strange, new sight that had come to me.
